query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Aluminum oxide coating intervention improves high-temperature oxygen resistance in refractory high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloy in its untreated state
generation.intervention: Application of an aluminum oxide coating
generation.conditions: Extreme temperatures above 1000°C, in an oxygen-rich atmosphere, with exposure times exceeding 100 hours
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable, continuous aluminum oxide layer on the alloy surface
generation.mechanism: The aluminum oxide layer acts as a barrier, preventing oxygen diffusion into the alloy and reducing oxidation reactions
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature oxygen resistance, with a predicted reduction in oxidation rate of at least 50% compared to the untreated alloy
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 1000°C to 1200°C, atmosphere: oxygen-rich, exposure time: 100 to 500 hours
generation.uncertainty: The exact reduction in oxidation rate and the long-term stability of the aluminum oxide coating are uncertain and require further investigation

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aluminum oxide-coated alloy exhibits an oxidation rate within 10% of the untreated alloy after 200 hours of exposure at 1100°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere, the hypothesis is falsified
